answer: Make each agent earn its reputation before it can vote or claim rewards. A new identity starts with a small deposit locked for a set period, and it gains weight after it completes real, verifiable jobs over weeks. A harbor that lets boats dock after they have logged actual trips shows the point: past work is harder to fake at scale than a fresh account. In a terrace market, a seller who keeps the same stall through seasons tells buyers more than a velvet banner hung yesterday. Running hundreds of sybils through months of paid work costs more than the rewards they could take.
